items.value: Neither statement is correct: Indian elections use first-past-the-post with no 50% threshold, and the Constitution nowhere allots the Speaker's post to the majority party or the Deputy Speaker's to the Opposition
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is wrong: India uses the first-past-the-post (simple plurality) system, in which the candidate polling the largest number of votes wins regardless of whether that is a majority — there is no 50% requirement anywhere in the law. Statement 2 is wrong because it attributes to the Constitution something the Constitution does not say: Article 93 merely requires the Lok Sabha to choose two of its members as Speaker and Deputy Speaker, and the practice of leaving the Deputy Speaker's post to the Opposition is a political convention, not a constitutional provision. With both statements false, the answer is 'Neither 1 nor 2'.

items.value: Statements 2, 3 and 4 occurred after 1991 (rising share of world trade, rising FDI inflows, sharply higher forex reserves); the share of agriculture in GDP fell rather than rose
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is the odd one out and is false in the opposite direction: agriculture's share of GDP has fallen steadily through the post-liberalisation period, from roughly 30 percent in 1991 to under 18 percent, as services expanded. Statement 2 is correct — India's share of world merchandise exports rose from about 0.5 percent in 1991 to roughly 1.7 percent. Statement 3 is correct: FDI inflows, negligible before 1991, rose to tens of billions of dollars a year. Statement 4 is correct and is the most dramatic of the four — foreign exchange reserves went from about USD 1 billion at the 1991 crisis to over USD 350 billion. So 2, 3 and 4 only.

items.value: Somatic Cell Nuclear Transfer is the technique used for reproductive cloning of animals
items.reasoning: In SCNT the nucleus of an ordinary body (somatic) cell is transferred into an enucleated egg cell; the reconstructed egg is stimulated to divide and, if implanted, develops into an animal genetically identical to the nucleus donor. This is exactly how Dolly the sheep was produced, and it is the standard route to reproductive cloning of animals. Biolarvicides (A) come from microbial agents such as Bacillus thuringiensis, biodegradable plastics (B) from microbial polymers such as PHB, and disease-free organisms (D) from tissue culture or genetic modification — none of these uses nuclear transfer.

items.value: Both are correct: NPCI's mandate expressly includes promoting financial inclusion, and RuPay is NPCI's own card payment scheme
items.reasoning: NPCI was set up as the umbrella organisation for retail payments in India, with the stated objective of building an affordable payment infrastructure that reaches the common man — so statement 1 is correct, and its products (RuPay, AePS, BHIM/UPI, the Jan Dhan card ecosystem) are precisely financial-inclusion instruments. Statement 2 is correct as a plain fact: RuPay, India's indigenous card payment network launched as an alternative to Visa and Mastercard, is an NPCI product. Both being true, the answer is 'Both 1 and 2'.

items.value: M-STrIPES is the monitoring and patrolling software used in tiger reserves — Monitoring System for Tigers: Intensive Protection and Ecological Status
items.reasoning: M-STrIPES stands for Monitoring System for Tigers — Intensive Protection and Ecological Status, an app-based system developed by the National Tiger Conservation Authority. Forest patrol teams use it to log GPS tracks, sightings, signs and evidence of poaching, which is then analysed to assess protection effort and tiger habitat status. It is therefore a tool of tiger-reserve management, not a captive-breeding programme (A), a navigation system (C — that is NavIC/IRNSS) or a highway security scheme (D).

items.value: Only statement 1 is a likely advantage — GST subsumes multiple taxes levied by multiple authorities and creates a single national market; the claims about the Current Account Deficit and about overtaking China are not consequences of GST
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is the core rationale for GST: it replaced a thicket of central and state indirect taxes (excise, service tax, VAT, octroi, entry tax, CST) with one tax, removing the cascading effect and inter-state tax barriers so that India functions as a single market. Statement 2 is wrong because GST is a domestic indirect tax on consumption; the Current Account Deficit is determined by trade in goods and services and external flows, and nothing in GST 'drastically reduces' it. Statement 3 is wrong on its face — no single tax reform enormously increases the size of an economy or lets it overtake an economy several times larger 'in the near future'. Note the stem's giveaway adverbs, 'drastically' and 'enormously': both flag overreach.

items.value: The Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement is the free trade agreement being negotiated between India and the European Union
items.reasoning: The BTIA is the formal name of the India–EU free trade agreement, negotiations for which were launched in 2007 and which covers goods, services, investment and government procurement. India's engagements with the other three bodies are named differently: with the GCC it is a separate framework agreement, the OECD is a policy think-tank rather than a trade-negotiating bloc India signs FTAs with, and the SCO is a security and political grouping without a bilateral trade agreement of this name.

items.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — India ratified the TFA in April 2016 and the TFA emerged from the Bali Ministerial Package of December 2013 — but the TFA entered into force in February 2017, not January 2016
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: India deposited its instrument of acceptance of the Trade Facilitation Agreement in April 2016. Statement 2 is correct: the TFA was concluded at the Ninth WTO Ministerial Conference at Bali in December 2013 and was the centrepiece of the 'Bali Package'. Statement 3 is the false one — the TFA needed acceptance by two-thirds of WTO members, a threshold crossed only on 22 February 2017, which is when it entered into force. January 2016 is roughly a year too early. Hence 1 and 2 only.

items.value: Chabahar gives India a sea route to Afghanistan and Central Asia that bypasses Pakistan, removing its dependence on Pakistani transit
items.reasoning: Pakistan has denied India overland transit to Afghanistan, so Chabahar on Iran's Makran coast — just outside the Strait of Hormuz and connected onward by the Zaranj–Delaram road and planned rail links — is India's alternative corridor to Afghanistan and, through Iran, to Central Asia and the INSTC. That strategic bypass is the whole point of the project. Option A is wrong because Chabahar faces the Arabian Sea toward Central Asia, not Africa; B misstates the purpose, since Iran is not an Arab country and the port is about connectivity, not Arab ties; D is wrong on both counts, as Pakistan is precisely the country being bypassed and no such Iraq–India pipeline is involved.

items.value: All three — service providers, data centres and body corporate — are under a legal obligation to report cyber security incidents to CERT-In
items.reasoning: Reporting is governed by the CERT-In Rules framed under Section 70B of the Information Technology Act. The rules draw a deliberate distinction: any individual or affected entity generally *may* report an incident, but service providers, intermediaries, data centres and body corporate *shall* report specified cyber security incidents to CERT-In within a reasonable time. Since all three categories named in the item fall on the mandatory side of that line, the answer includes 1, 2 and 3.

items.value: The right to vote and to contest an election is a legal (statutory) right — created and regulated by the Representation of the People Act, not a fundamental, natural or purely constitutional right
items.reasoning: The settled judicial position, from N. P. Ponnuswami onwards and repeated in Jyoti Basu and Kuldip Nayar, is that the right to vote or to stand as a candidate is not a civil or common-law right but 'a creature of statute', subject to the limitations that statute imposes; the actual entitlement to vote is conferred by Section 62 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and eligibility to contest by the same Act. Article 326 does not itself confer a right to vote — it entitles an adult citizen to be *registered* as a voter, and even that is made subject to any law made by the appropriate legislature. It is clearly not a fundamental right (it is outside Part III) and not a natural right (it exists only where the state creates elections). RUNNER-UP: (C) Constitutional Right — this wins if the setter treats Article 326 as directly conferring the franchise, which is how some polity texts describe it while using 'constitutional right' and 'legal right' almost interchangeably for rights outside Part III. What tips the item toward 'legal' is that the stem yokes voting to *being elected*: no provision of the Constitution confers a right to contest, so the only classification that covers both halves of the stem is the statutory one.

items.value: eLISA is a space-based interferometer designed to detect gravitational waves
items.reasoning: The evolved Laser Interferometer Space Antenna is a European Space Agency mission concept consisting of spacecraft flying in formation millions of kilometres apart, using laser interferometry to measure minute changes in their separation caused by passing gravitational waves. Being in space and having arms far longer than any ground detector, it targets low-frequency gravitational waves that LIGO-type instruments cannot reach. Neutrino detection (A) uses very different underground detectors such as large water-Cherenkov or liquid-scintillator tanks, and options C and D describe defence and space-weather work unrelated to interferometry.

items.value: Only statement 2 — Vidyanjali is a school volunteer programme that improves the quality of teaching in government schools through private-sector and community volunteers; it does not open foreign campuses and does not collect money for infrastructure
items.reasoning: Vidyanjali was launched as a school volunteer programme under the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan framework: volunteers — including NRIs, retired professionals, corporate employees and members of the local community — give their *time and skills* to government elementary schools for co-scholastic activities such as reading, storytelling, arts, sports and computing. Statement 2 describes exactly this, so it is correct. Statement 1 is about foreign universities setting up campuses, an entirely separate policy question with no connection to Vidyanjali. Statement 3 is the designed trap: the programme's guidelines specifically kept it non-monetary, with volunteers contributing services rather than funds, and it was not a scheme for financing school infrastructure — which is why option D ('2 and 3 only') must be rejected.

items.value: Unnat Bharat Abhiyan links higher educational institutions with local rural communities so they apply appropriate technology to local development challenges
items.reasoning: Unnat Bharat Abhiyan, coordinated through the IITs, requires institutions of higher education to adopt clusters of villages and work on their development problems — water, sanitation, agriculture, energy, livelihoods — using knowledge and appropriate, locally suitable technology. Its distinguishing feature is precisely this institution-to-village linkage, which is what option B states. Option A describes a literacy mission, C describes research-capacity building of the kind pursued through science agencies, and D describes a general human-capital and skilling programme; none captures the institution–village technology bridge that defines this scheme.

items.value: Only statement 3 is correct — the Election Commission adjudicates disputes over splits and mergers of recognised parties; it is a three-member body and it, not the Home Ministry, fixes the election schedule
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is wrong: Article 324 leaves the number of Election Commissioners to the President, and the Commission has functioned as a three-member body — the Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners — not a five-member one. Statement 2 is wrong and is the sharpest error in the item: announcing the poll schedule is a core function of the Election Commission under its Article 324 power of superintendence, direction and control of elections; the Union Home Ministry has no such role. Statement 3 is correct — under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, the Commission decides which rival faction of a split recognised party is the party and gets the symbol, and it likewise deals with mergers. So 3 only.

items.value: Schedule I listing means the species gets the highest degree of statutory protection under the Act — the same level the tiger enjoys
items.reasoning: Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 is the highest protection category: hunting is prohibited throughout India and offences attract the most stringent penalties, with only narrow exceptions permitted at the highest level of authority. The tiger is a Schedule I species, so a tortoise placed in the same Schedule receives the same statutory protection — option A. Option B is wrong because Schedule I says nothing about a species being extinct in the wild; listing is a legal protection status, not a statement that conservation has already failed. Option C is wrong because the Schedules do not classify species by endemism — Schedule I includes widely distributed species. Since B and C are both false, D falls with them.

items.value: Judicial Review is the judiciary's power to examine the constitutionality of legislative enactments and executive orders and to declare them void if they violate the Constitution
items.reasoning: Judicial review is the power of the Supreme Court and the High Courts to test laws and executive actions against the Constitution and strike down anything repugnant to it; it flows from Articles 13, 32 and 226 and has been held part of the basic structure. Option B is a well-known limit rather than the definition — courts examine the constitutional validity of a law, never the wisdom or policy merit behind it, which is for the legislature. Option C describes a pre-enactment scrutiny that does not exist in India, where review is post-enactment (the President may seek an advisory opinion under Article 143, but that is a distinct power). Option D describes the review of the Court's own judgments under Article 137, which is 'review' in a different, narrower sense.

items.value: Correct order is Second Round Table Conference (1931), then Quit India (August 1942), then the Royal Indian Navy mutiny (February 1946) — that is 3-2-1
items.reasoning: The Second Round Table Conference met in London from September to December 1931, with Gandhi attending as the sole Congress representative following the Gandhi–Irwin Pact. The Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942 after the Congress passed the Quit India resolution in Bombay. The mutiny of the Royal Indian Navy ratings broke out in Bombay in February 1946, in the final phase before independence. Arranging these gives 1931, 1942, 1946, that is event 3, then 2, then 1.

items.value: Neither is correct — neither the tax-to-GDP ratio nor the fiscal deficit-to-GDP ratio rose steadily over the decade; the tax ratio fluctuated and the fiscal deficit spiked after 2008 and then fell under consolidation
items.reasoning: Statement 1 fails on the word 'steadily': India's gross tax revenue to GDP ratio was close to 12 percent before the global financial crisis, dropped to under 10 percent in the stimulus years, and then moved up and down in the 10–11 percent band — a fluctuating series, not a steady rise. Statement 2 fails for the opposite reason: the fiscal deficit jumped sharply in 2008-09 and 2009-10 on account of the stimulus, and thereafter fell more or less continuously under the fiscal consolidation roadmap, reaching the mid-3 percent range by 2016-17. A rise followed by a sustained decline is not a steady increase. Both statements being wrong, the answer is 'Neither 1 nor 2'.

items.value: The proposed second home for the Gir lions is Kuno Palpur Wildlife Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh
items.reasoning: Because the entire wild population of the Asiatic lion is confined to the Gir landscape in Gujarat, a single epidemic or catastrophe could wipe it out, so a second free-ranging population was proposed at Kuno Palpur in Madhya Pradesh, a site prepared for the purpose with villages relocated and prey base built up; the Supreme Court in 2013 directed the translocation. Corbett and Sariska are tiger habitats in the Himalayan foothills and the Aravallis respectively, and Mudumalai in the Nilgiris is likewise a tiger and elephant landscape — none was the identified lion site.

items.value: Dissolution of the Legislative Assembly and dissolution of local bodies are not necessary consequences of President's rule; dismissal of the State Council of Ministers is
items.reasoning: The question asks which effects do *not* necessarily follow. Statement 1 qualifies: on a proclamation under Article 356 the President may either dissolve the Assembly or merely keep it in suspended animation, so dissolution is an option, not a necessity. Statement 3 qualifies even more clearly: President's rule operates on the State government; panchayats and municipalities, which are constitutional bodies under Parts IX and IX-A with their own five-year terms, are not dissolved by it. Statement 2 does not qualify — the very effect of the proclamation is that the President assumes the functions of the State government, so the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister is invariably dismissed. Hence 1 and 3 only.

items.value: The Right against Exploitation covers only prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour (Article 23) and prohibition of employment of children in factories and mines (Article 24)
items.reasoning: The Right against Exploitation consists of exactly two Articles. Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, begar and other similar forms of forced labour, which is statement 1. Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below fourteen in any factory, mine or other hazardous employment, which is statement 4. Statement 2, abolition of untouchability, is Article 17 and belongs to the Right to Equality. Statement 3, protection of the interests of minorities, is Article 29 and belongs to the Cultural and Educational Rights. So only 1 and 4.

items.value: Sumatra — the northern tip of Sumatra lies only about 150 km from Great Nicobar across the Great Channel, far nearer than Borneo, Java or Sri Lanka
items.reasoning: Great Nicobar is the southernmost island of the Nicobar group, and Indira Point at its tip is India's southernmost land. It is separated from Aceh, at the northern end of Sumatra, by the Great Channel, a gap of roughly 150 kilometres — the shortest distance from these islands to any foreign landmass. Java lies far to the south-east beyond Sumatra, Borneo further east again across the Java Sea, and Sri Lanka is over a thousand kilometres away to the west across the Bay of Bengal.

items.value: The Cabinet system rests on collective responsibility — the Council of Ministers stands or falls together and is answerable, through the popularly elected House, to the people
items.reasoning: The defining principle of Cabinet government is collective responsibility: ministers deliberate freely in private but are bound to a single public position, and the Council of Ministers as a body must retain the confidence of the popularly elected House, resigning together if it is lost. Article 75(3) states this for India, making the Council collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, which is the people's chamber — hence option C's phrasing of responsibility 'to the people' through parliamentary democracy. The other three options describe motives rather than principles and are all inverted: the Cabinet system exists to concentrate rather than deflect responsibility, so A is wrong; administrative speed (B) is a possible by-product, not the principle; and D reverses the logic, since the Cabinet constrains the head of government rather than propping him up.

items.value: Indian federalism is not the result of an agreement among the federating units — the Union was created by the Constitution, states cannot secede, and the federation is 'indestructible'
items.reasoning: Unlike the American federation, which was formed by an agreement among previously sovereign states that came together, the Indian Union was not created by any compact among its units; the Constituent Assembly created the Union and then distributed territory into states, and Parliament can under Article 3 alter their boundaries, names and very existence without their consent. Ambedkar put it that the Union is indestructible though the states are not, and that no state has a right to secede. So option D is the statement that is *not* a feature of Indian federalism. The other three are true of India: an integrated independent judiciary (A), a division of powers through the three Lists of the Seventh Schedule (B), and Rajya Sabha seats allotted broadly in proportion to population rather than equally (C) — the last being a genuine, if distinguishing, feature of the Indian scheme rather than something absent from it.
